did_you_know.text: Did you know? When the wall of Jerusalem began to be rebuilt and the breaches were being repaired, it aroused the anger of Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites.
Did you know? Nehemiah and the people did not rely on prayer alone: they also posted a guard over Jerusalem day and night because of their enemies.

Did you know? Judah described the difficulty of the work with the words, “The strength of the laborers is failing”—the workers carrying the building materials had grown weak, and there was a great deal of rubble.
Did you know? Jews living among the surrounding nations repeatedly warned Nehemiah—“ten times”—about places from which an attack might come.
Did you know? Nehemiah organized the people by families and stationed them in defensive positions, equipped with swords, spears, and bows.
Did you know? Nehemiah encouraged the people not to be afraid, to remember the great and awesome Lord, and to fight for their brothers, sons, daughters, wives, and homes.
Did you know? Jerusalem’s defense was integrated with the rebuilding work: half of the people worked, while the other half held spears, shields, bows, and armor.
Did you know? Some of the builders worked with their swords strapped to their waists, while a man who sounded the trumpet stood beside Nehemiah to summon the people when necessary.
Did you know? Because the builders were spread out along a wide section of the wall, it was decided that everyone who heard the sound of the trumpet would gather at the place where help was needed.

Did you know? The preparations continued outside working hours as well: the people and the young men spent the night inside Jerusalem; the night was devoted to guarding, and the day to working, while the guards remained ready with their weapons.
